hints: Look at the list 1 to 4 and ask yourself, which of these polysaccharides are branched and which are straight chains?
Remember that 1,4 bonds make the straight chain, while 1,6 bonds are only needed to make a branch point, so only branched polysaccharides will have both.
walkthrough:
**Spot what the bonds mean**

Think of it simply. A 1,4 glycosidic bond joins glucose molecules end to end to make a chain. A 1,6 glycosidic bond creates a side branch off that chain.

So to have BOTH types, the polysaccharide must be branched.

**Sort the four polysaccharides**

Amylopectin (1) is the branched form of starch. Glycogen (4) is the highly branched storage polysaccharide in animals.

Amylose (2) is the unbranched, coiled form of starch. Cellulose (3) is a straight, unbranched chain of beta-glucose. Those two only need 1,4 bonds.

**Pick the correct combination**

Only 1 and 4 are branched, so only 1 and 4 contain both 1,4 and 1,6 bonds. That matches option B.

options.A: Incorrect because cellulose (3) is unbranched and has only 1,4 beta-glycosidic bonds, no 1,6 bonds.
options.B: Correct because both amylopectin (1) and glycogen (4) are branched, with 1,4 bonds in the chains and 1,6 bonds at branch points.
options.C: Incorrect because both amylose (2) and cellulose (3) are unbranched and contain only 1,4 glycosidic bonds.
options.D: Incorrect because glycogen (4) is correct, but amylopectin (1) also has both bond types, so it is not 4 only.
